title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
wiki_lead:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a 1998 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It was the first Legend of Zelda game with 3D graphics. It was released in Japan and North America in November 1998 and in PAL regions the following month.
Ocarina of Time was developed by Nintendo's Entertainment Analysis & Development division. It was led by five directors, including Eiji Aonuma and Yoshiaki Koizumi, produced by series co-creator Shigeru Miyamoto, and written by Kensuke Tanabe. Series composer Koji Kondo wrote its soundtrack. The player controls Link in the kingdom of Hyrule on a quest to stop the evil Gerudo king Ganondorf by traveling through time and navigating dungeons and an overworld. The game introduced features such as a target-lock system and context-sensitive buttons, which have since become common in 3D adventure games. The player must play songs on an ocarina to progress.
Ocarina of Time was acclaimed by critics, who praised its visuals, sound, gameplay, soundtrack, and writing. It has been ranked by numerous publications as one of the greatest video games and is the highest-rated game on the review aggregators Metacritic and GameRankings. It set a record for video game pre-orders in the US and sold more than seven million copies worldwide.
Ocarina of Time has been rereleased on every Nintendo home console and on the iQue Player in China. Some releases include Master Quest, an alternative version including new puzzles and increased difficulty. A sequel, Majora's Mask, was released for the Nintendo 64 in 2000. A remake for the Nintendo 3DS, Ocarina of Time 3D, was released in 2011. A second remake for the Nintendo Switch 2 was released on November 5, 2026.

Gameplay

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a fantasy action-adventure game set in a 3D world with an expansive environment. The game world is mostly rendered in real-time polygonal 3D, while a few areas make use of pre-rendered backgrounds. The player controls Link from a third-person perspective. Link primarily fights with a sword and shield but can also use other weapons such as projectiles, bombs, and magic spells.
The control scheme introduced techniques such as context-sensitive actions and a targeting system called "Z-targeting", which allows the player to have Link focus on enemies or objects. When using this technique, the camera follows the target and Link constantly faces it. Projectile attacks are automatically directed at the target and do not require manual aiming. Context-sensitive actions allow multiple tasks to be assigned to one button, simplifying the control scheme. The on-screen display shows what will happen when the button is pushed and changes depending on what the character is doing. For example, the button that causes Link to push a box if he is standing next to it will have him climb on the box if the analog stick is pushed toward it. grok_lead: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a 1998 action-adventure video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64 console. In it, players control the young hero Link, who embarks on a quest through the kingdom of Hyrule and across time to thwart the evil Gerudo king Ganondorf's plan to seize the Triforce âa sacred relic granting immense powerâand plunge the land into darkness. First released in Japan on November 21, 1998, and in North America on November 23, 1998, the game introduced groundbreaking 3D gameplay mechanics to the series, including real-time combat, puzzle-solving, and exploration in a vast open world. The game's narrative unfolds in two timelines: Link's childhood, where he collects three Spiritual Stones to access the Sacred Realm, and his adult years seven years later, after being sealed away by the Master Sword, during which Hyrule falls under Ganondorf's rule. Players wield a variety of weapons and items, such as the titular ocarinaâa magical flute used to manipulate time and weatherâand engage in epic boss battles against formidable foes. The title's innovative lock-on targeting system, known as "Z-targeting," revolutionized action gameplay by allowing fluid navigation and combat in three dimensions. Developed by Nintendo's Entertainment Analysis & Development (EAD) division under director Shigeru Miyamoto, Ocarina of Time drew inspiration from earlier Zelda titles while pushing the boundaries of the Nintendo 64 hardware. It received universal critical acclaim upon release, earning a Metascore of 99 out of 100 based on 22 reviews, making it the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic. The title won multiple prestigious awards, including Game of the Year and Console Game of the Year at the 2nd Annual Interactive Achievement Awards, as well as a BAFTA Interactive Entertainment Award. Widely regarded as a landmark in video game history, Ocarina of Time has influenced countless titles with its blend of epic storytelling, immersive world-building, and accessible yet deep mechanics, and it remains a benchmark for the action-adventure genre. A remastered version, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D, was later released for the Nintendo 3DS in 2011, enhancing visuals and adding features like the 3DS's stereoscopic 3D display. A ground-up remake for the Nintendo Switch 2, featuring completely overhauled visuals, fully voiced cutscenes, and modernized controls, was released on November 5, 2026.
